references.text: Abraham asked the three guests to stay with him when they were nearby, in a similar way that the disciples will soon ask Jesus to stay with them. The motif of hospitality – inviting a traveler to stop – is common to both texts ([ref:1 Mos 18:3-5|Genesis 18:3-5]).

Jacob refused to let go of the angel and said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me." This recalls how Jesus pretends he intends to go further, thereby provoking the disciples' eagerness to hold him back ([ref:1 Mos 32:26|Genesis 32:26]).
The immediately following verse shows the disciples' reaction: they urge him to stay, which is the direct response to Jesus pretending he intended to go further ([ref:Luk 24:29|Luke 24:29]).

Jesus came walking on the sea toward the disciples and "intended to pass by them" (παρελθεῖν). Here too, Jesus pretends he intends to continue onward, which parallels Luke 24:28 where he pretends he is going further ([ref:Mark 6:48|Mark 6:48]).

Lot insisted that the two angels stay overnight with him instead of continuing on. The motif of heavenly guests pretending they intend to go further, and a host urging them to stay, is found in Luke 24:28-29 ([ref:1 Mos 19:2-3|Genesis 19:2-3]).

Earlier in the same account, Jesus joined two disciples on the road, but their eyes were kept from recognizing him. That he now pretends to go further is a continuation of this hidden-presence motif ([ref:Luk 24:15-16|Luke 24:15-16]).
